bib.title: The specious art of single-cell genomics

read.skipped: Supporting information S1 Text (methods, Figs A-ZA, Tables A-B, Note) is not in the PDF; methods details live there.

question: How faithfully do 2D t-SNE/UMAP embeddings (after PCA preprocessing) of single-cell gene expression preserve local neighbourhoods, global structure and distances, and what does that do to the inferences drawn from them?
hypothesis: Extreme reduction from hundreds or thousands of dimensions to 2 inevitably distorts the data, so embeddings are counter-productive for exploratory biological analysis.
contributions: Quantify distortion of local (kNN Jaccard), global (cell-type neighbour ranking) and distance (max/min ratio) properties in 2D embeddings
Show distortion changes conclusions in integration, clustering, density, and trajectory applications
Introduce 'Picasso', an autoencoder that fits cells to arbitrary 2D shapes (elephant, flower) with fidelity similar to t-SNE/UMAP
Propose targeted alternatives (analysis in ambient or higher-dimensional space, L1 metric, MCML embeddings, dendrograms, heatmaps)

method.summary: Re-analysis of public single-cell RNA-seq datasets. Cells are reduced ambient -> PCA (e.g. 50D) -> 2D t-SNE/UMAP and distortion is measured against ambient and PCA spaces using neighbour overlap, rank correlation, distance ratios, label prediction and mixing fractions. Most methods are in the S1 Text, which this PDF does not contain.
method.task: Evaluating dimensionality-reduction distortion for single-cell exploratory analysis

datasets.name: Mouse VMH neurons (10x and SMART-Seq)
datasets.preprocessing: Highly variable gene selection and log-normalisation (ambient space)

datasets.name: Ex utero (E8.5) and ex/in utero (E10.5) mouse embryo

models.name: Picasso autoencoder
models.architecture: autoencoder fitting cells to an arbitrary 2D shape while preserving ambient distances

inference.samples: Embeddings generated n = 3 times (Fig 2B); n = 5 embeddings (Fig 7); n = 5 random subsets of 1,000 HVGs from top 2,000 HVGs (Fig 8)

parameters.pca_dims: 50 in the main example; other dimensions also tried
parameters.label_prediction: 30% of dataset predicted from labels of 50 nearest neighbours (Fig 4A)
parameters.distance_metrics: L2 default; L1 in S1 Text

metrics.name: Jaccard distance of 30-NN sets
metrics.definition: Jaccard dissimilarity between each cell's 30 nearest neighbours in the embedding and in ambient (or PCA) space; 1.0 = no overlap

metrics.name: Cell-type neighbour ranking correlation
metrics.definition: Correlation of rankings of cell-type neighbours built from average pairwise distances between types, versus ambient or PCA space

metrics.name: max/min distance ratio
metrics.definition: Ratio of maximum to minimum distance within groups of equidistant cells or nearest neighbours, embedding vs source space

metrics.name: Neighbour label prediction
metrics.definition: Predict a cell's label (type or condition) for 30% of the data from labels of 50 nearest neighbours

metrics.name: Mixing fraction
metrics.definition: Fraction of each cell's nearest neighbours with the cell's own condition label; 1.0 = no mixing

metrics.name: K-S distance between inter- and intra-type distance distributions
metrics.definition: Separation of cell types; higher = greater separation

metrics.name: Relative contrast (L1 vs L2)
metrics.definition: Ratio from Aggarwal et al. 2001 of an Lk norm's ability to separate near from far in high dimension

eval.protocol: Distances compared to ambient and PCA spaces, L2 default and L1 repeated; no significance tests stated in main text.

availability.data: Original data links in Table A of S1 Text; processed matrices on CaltechData (Table B)

results.claim: Mean Jaccard distance of 30-NN sets between PCA-preprocessed 2D t-SNE/UMAP and ambient space is above 0.7 across datasets.
results.setup: VMH 10x and SMART-Seq, E8.5, E10.5 embryos, MOp, mESC, 96-plex NSC; PCA-50D -> UMAP/t-SNE; L2, k=30
results.quote:
The 2D t-SNE/UMAP embeddings (e.g., “PCA-50D!UMAP” in Fig 2A) displayed large
Jaccard distances with respect to the neighbors in ambient dimension, with an average consis-
tently above 0.7 (70%).

results.claim: Jaccard distance between the 2D embedding and its own PCA space is also above 0.8 on average, whatever the initial PCA dimension.
results.setup: Same datasets; 2D vs relevant PCA space
results.quote:
Jaccard distances were consistently above 0.8 on average, regardless of the dimension of the initial
PCA reduction (Fig 2Aii

results.claim: Dissimilarity grows with dataset size, and 2D PCA is sometimes worse than t-SNE/UMAP at neighbour retention.
results.setup: Fig 2A, Figs A and B S1 Text
results.quote: Generally, dissimilarity increased with the size of the dataset

results.claim: Cell-type neighbour-ranking correlation to ambient is low (<=0.4) in PCA-preprocessed 2D embeddings, at least 33% lower than PCA spaces, with warped or reversed ranks.
results.setup: Same datasets plus human monocytes 40 drugs; ranks from average pairwise distance between cell types over replicate embeddings (n = 3)
results.note: The inequality sign before 0.4 is lost in the text extraction; the paper reads as 'low (<=0.4)' by inference.

results.claim: Johnson-Lindenstrauss: preserving pairwise distances within 20% error for 10,000 cells needs at least 1,842 dimensions.
Distortion of max/min distance ratio for n points in 2D grows as O(sqrt(n)).
results.setup: Theory: n points embedded in 2 dimensions
results.note: Quote is the garbled math fragment; value null.

results.claim: In 2D embeddings, max/min distance ratios rise 4- to 200-fold versus PCA or ambient space.
results.setup: E10.5 ex/in utero and 10x VMH neurons; equidistant groups and NN groups
results.quote: revealed 4- to 200-fold increases in these ratios

results.claim: Upwards of 2.5 million groups of 3 to 8 equidistant cells ('near' or 'far' in ambient space) in E10.5 data appear with the same dispersion in UMAP, so near and far are indistinguishable.
results.quote: This revealed upwards of 2.5 million such groups, with 3 to 8 cells in each

results.claim: The mixing of ex/in utero cells reverses between ambient space and UMAP depending on normalisation: well-mixed ambient becomes unmixed in 2D, and unmixed ambient becomes well-mixed.
results.setup: E10.5 integrated; log-normalised vs variance-stabilised and scaled
results.quote:
the distribution generated from embedding
into 2 dimensions was shifted towards unmixed

results.claim: MNN and Scanorama give similar mixing of CEL-Seq cells in ambient space but UMAP shows opposite pictures (MNN well-mixed, Scanorama unmixed).
results.setup: Pancreatic islet SMART-Seq2 + CEL-Seq; UMAP and t-SNE; L1 repeats
results.quote:
However
the UMAP embeddings provide opposite pictures

results.claim: Neighbour-based cell-label prediction is consistently worse in the 2D embedding than in higher-dimensional representations, even with supervised UMAP.
results.setup: VMH, E10.5, developing brain, 96-plex NSC; 30% held out, 50 nearest neighbours
results.quote:
is consistently worse in the 2D embedding space
than in higher dimensional representations, even when labels are given as with supervised
UMAP

results.claim: 2D reduction can narrow or widen the gap between inter- and intra-type distance distributions depending on dataset, so cluster separation in plots is not reliable.
results.quote:
reducing the gap
between inter-, intra-type distributions for some datasets and increasing the gap for others

results.claim: Cluster structure is highly sensitive to n_neighbors / perplexity; common choices (1% to 10% of data) move progenitors away or merge distinct early populations.
results.setup: E10.5 data, Fig P S1 Text
results.quote:
cluster structures were additionally highly sensitive to the number of neigh-
bors (perplexity for t-SNE)

results.claim: Scanpy and Seurat feed the same PCA-space kNN graph to both clustering and embedding, so the embedding is not an independent check of the clustering.
results.quote:
the same k-nearest neighbor (kNN) graph constructed from the higher
dimensional PCA space is passed to both the clustering algorithm and the embedding algorithm

results.claim: Changing n_neighbors from 5 to 50 (UMAP) or perplexity 5 to 50 (t-SNE) creates and removes condition-specific populations and changes apparent density scale.
results.setup: E10.5 ex vs in utero, Fig 5
results.quote: can result in dramatic appearances of cell populations present in 1 condition but not the other

results.claim: Picasso autoencoder embeds cells in an elephant or flower shape with inter-/intra-type distance correlations comparable to t-SNE/UMAP and better intra-type correlations.
results.setup: E8.5, MERFISH MOp, SMART-Seq VMH; n = 5 embeddings
results.quote:
Each Picasso embedding demonstrated comparable performance to t-SNE and
UMAP (Fig 7)

results.claim: L1 has higher relative contrast than L2 across datasets in gene space.
results.setup: n = 5 random subsets of 1,000 HVGs from top 2,000; Fig 8
results.quote:
We found that L1 has higher contrast values than the L2
norm across datasets (Fig 8)

results.claim: UMAP transform of uniformly distributed high-dim points using coordinates fit on a single-cell dataset imposes a false structure resembling that dataset.
results.quote: imposes a false structure akin to the structure of the single-cell data

limits: Methods, per-dataset sizes, and most supporting figures are in S1 Text, not in this PDF.
Perspective piece: no significance tests in the main text; most results are qualitative or read from figures.
Authors concede 2D embeddings 'can reflect the broader strokes of the data such as cell type inter-distances'.
Theory (JL, O(sqrt n)) concerns distance preservation; t-SNE/UMAP aim mainly at local structure, though local neighbour overlap was also poor.
The PCA-then-embed pipeline is the focus; pure 2D from ambient was also poor but sometimes slightly different.
Alternatives (MCML, relative contrast) are only sketched; role of dataset features in contrast values is 'unexplored'.
Single-cell RNA-seq data only; carryover to other tabular segmentation data is an inference.
practices: Do not use 2D t-SNE/UMAP for quantitative claims about distances, density, mixing, or trajectories; treat as cartoon diagrams displayed post-analysis (Discussion).
Cluster in higher-dimensional PCA space or ambient space, not on 2D coordinates (Discussion, p.15).
Validate clusters with heatmaps of marker features, not the embedding (p.15).
Use dendrograms, trees or graph diagrams for between-cluster relationships (p.15).
Consider L1 over L2 for high-dimensional distances; pick the metric before any reduction (p.14).
Limit dimensionality reduction and ad hoc transforms when the space of interest can be treated directly (p.15).
